title: reading notes: KV cache & memory optimizations for LLM inference
content:
2026-02-18 notes (ongoing)

Quick summary:
- Goal: collect practical takeaways from recent papers/blogs about KV cache, memory layout, and session state for transformer inference. Focus on production tradeoffs: latency, memory footprint, GC/eviction, and multi-tenant isolation.
- Intended for: implementation in serving runtime + dedicated GPU pools (Redwood Dedicated).

Papers & posts scanned (fast pass):
- FlashAttention / memory-aware attention optimizations (paper + impl notes) — important for reducing host<->GPU memory pressure when computing attention for long contexts.
- K-V cache sharding and prefix caching (various arXiv examples + OSS PRs) — tradeoffs on per-token latency vs. memory.
- Continuous / incremental KV cache update strategies (blog posts + GH issues) — helpful for streaming and long-lived sessions.

Key notes / takeaways (rough):
- Memory layout matters: flattened contiguous KV tensors (per-layer) are much faster for memcpy and GPU scatter/gather than per-token lists. Align to 256B for GPU DMA.
- Sharding strategy: prefer model-layer-based sharding across GPUs when possible (per-layer KV owned by GPU that serves that layer) to avoid cross-device fetches on every token. But increases complexity for model parallel configs.
- Eviction policies: LRU too heavy for large sessions; use TTL + size thresholds + sampling-based eviction for background compaction. Keep small fast-path for recent prefixes used by streaming.
- Compression / quantization: quantized KV (int8/4bit) reduces memory 2-4x. Need to benchmark inference fidelity: for KV values quant noise can propagate across many decoding steps. Consider hybrid: store keys quantized, values float16 or bf16 for critical layers.
- Caching at different granularities: prefix-level (full sequence) vs. chunk-level. Chunk-level (fixed window) reduces memory but requires recomputing previous attention for overlap windows -> extra compute.
- Consistency for rollbacks and A/B rollouts: version KV cache objects with model-version tag. When routing falls back to smaller model, KV formats might differ -> need canonical conversion or forced recompute.

Implementation experiments to run (prioritized):
1) Microbench: contiguous per-layer KV vs. interleaved per-token layout. Measure memcpy + kernel launch times for 1k, 8k, 32k contexts on A100 and H100.
2) Quantized KV store: try int8 keys + fp16 values; measure memory, latency, and generation divergence on standard prompts (eval set).
3) Sharding test: run 2 configs (layer-shard vs. sequence-shard) with simulated multi-tenant workload to measure cross-GPU PCIe/NVLink traffic and tail latency.
4) Eviction TTL heuristic: implement sampling-based compaction and compare to LRU under churn (many short sessions + a few long sessions).

Operational considerations for Redwood:
- Observability: expose KV store size per session, per-model, per-GPU; track cache-hit rate for prefix reuse and cost-savings.
- Billing: double-counted memory across tenants in dedicated pools? We should attribute KV memory to requests/clients to reflect cost-per-session.
- Security: ensure KV persistence (if any) respects customer data isolation; scrub sensitive tokens from caches (PII detection heuristics).
- Rolling upgrades: provide safe migration path for KV format (versioned metadata + on-read conversion fallback).

Open questions / unknowns:
- How much model accuracy/regression comes from quantizing K vs. V tensors separately? Need systematic eval.
- Best tradeoffs for prefix caching for chat applications with many short prefixes vs. few very long ones.
- Memory reclaim vs. fragmentation on GPU for dynamic KV stores (cudaMalloc/free fragmentation). Investigate custom allocator + pooling.

Short TODOs (me + Maya):
- [ ] sketch microbench harness (1 day) + define metrics (throughput, p50/p95 latency, memcpy time).
- [ ] spin up small cluster test for sharding experiment (req infra help; tag Ethan). -> TODO create INF-679 ticket.
- [ ] prototype quantized-KV store in runtime branch (gh: kv-cache-proto/pull/42).
- [ ] draft Confluence design doc: link to existing draft and expand section on eviction policies.

Notes to self (brain dump):
- Keep experiments reproducible: record CUDA driver version, NCCL, PyTorch/TensorRT versions.
- For live demos, pick two customer-like patterns: chat app (many short sessions) and summarization (few long sessions) to show delta.
- Check with SRE about memory limits and OOM handling semantics in Dedicated nodes (graceful degrade vs. kill).

References / quick links:
- FlashAttention (paper + impl) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.14111
- KV cache design katamari PR — https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache-proto/pull/42
- Internal design draft — https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/KV+Cache+Design
- SRE slack thread about OOM behaviour — SLACK:#serving-runtime thread ts=1700000000

End of notes for now. Will add microbench results and paste charts here once done.

-- Aaron
